messages.subject: Trouble with unknown distances
parts:
Hello everybody! I'd like to have some good news, but again I'm in trouble and hope that sombody will come to the rescue :-)
In my data, I have maybe 30% of sightings with unknown distance from transect, and unfortunately I have to include them in the calculations.
When I just add them to the middle bin, here is what happens:


That's why I'd like to simulate the distance for these observations. Is there a simple way to do it in R? Can I use the previously fitted half-normal to distribute them?

Best regards,
Piotr Sadowski
Baltic Trade and Invest

messages.author: 9b03386432b784c0
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Trouble with unknown distances
parts:
Hi Piotr, list,

As I see it, there's no point in simulating distances to then fit detection functions to them. I assume you have no covariates besides distance (things can get messier otherwise!).

It seems easier to just assume that those distances miss at random with respect to distance value and then use only those those observations for which you do have distances for to fit the detection function. Then, assume that the same detection function applies to all observations (with and without distances) and use all the observations for the encounter rate.

I am not sure what is the best way in Distance to define this procedure, but I seem to recall that there's a way you can use detection functions fit to a subset of data to provide detectability information for all the data. Others?

have a good weekend!

Cheers,

T
